correctness.rationale: Equal rates give a uniform next available triple and P(2 from X)=(X-1)/(s-2). For d=X-Y the conditional mean contracts by (s-3)/(s-2); the product p_k is the displayed gamma ratio and is uniformly asymptotic to (s_k/(2n))^(1/3) at both cutoffs (shifting the lower cutoff by at most two sites is immaterial). The stopped martingale d_k/p_k has variance O(n) and absorption above n^(1/2)-3 would require magnitude of order at least n^(2/3), hence has probability O(n^(-1/3)). To the upper cutoff, the deterministic variance sum is asymptotic to 2n by a mesh-three integral; the expected imbalance correction is O(n^(1/2)), and the normalized maximum step is o(1), giving the martingale CLT. The further normalized variance to n^(1/8) is O(n^(-1/6)); Doob controls the entire interval. Survival to that lower cutoff forces normalized imbalance o(1), an event of vanishing probability because the frozen Gaussian has no atom at zero. At absorption within the interval R_n=|d| and hence |d/p_k|/sqrt(2n)=(R_n/(2n)^(1/4))^(2/3)(1+o(1)). The CDF and density follow. 'Unique terminal state' is read per trajectory, not as a deterministic common configuration. `python3 /workspace/reproduce.py` independently checked the labeled transitions for n=2..6; at n=6 it gave R=0 with probability 25/28 and R=3 with probability 3/28. This is not a simulation proof of the limit.
